account:
Today has mostly followed ordinary town business: my morning market walk, lunch at home, an attempted accounts review, and now tea with my neighbour. Residents I asked had no confirmed news. The neighbour personally confirmed this cottage beside the east ferry landing, and I have arrived just after three; they are waiting nearby.

There was some confusion over the tea address. The secretary searched dockside cottages and asked warehouse workers, then repeatedly asked me to confirm the host and location. Several of my replies were missed while we were apart or moving. Eventually the secretary acknowledged the exact address. I have no evidence this was anything more than a communication problem.

The main new business is the innkeeper's community gathering tomorrow at eighteen hundred in the town hall's great hall. I approved attending, and the secretary said the appointment has been recorded and stored with the appointment book. The innkeeper also requested a private conversation with the secretary about catering, clarifying that the question was for the secretary rather than me. This seems to be preparation for the gathering; I do not know the catering details, and privacy alone gives me no reason to infer anything improper.

The accounts review could not proceed properly: the secretary had received no figures and asked where the ledger was. I did not know. I checked the treasury chest and found two stacks of 64 emeralds, but no ledger. That leaves the accounts review unfinished; I have not observed any shortage or evidence of wrongdoing. After tea, my next scheduled office appointment is at sixteen thirty.
